text: Helen is a renter, a queer woman, and a TV writer who can't stay away from local advocacy. It started when she was living in New Orleans during the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina. As president of the local neighborhood association, she helped create desperately needed housing for displaced residents by working with the city, neighbors, developers, and the historic district.

The project she's most proud of is helping turn an underutilized historic warehouse into 37 units of affordable apartments for working artists and musicians. Those apartments still exist, they're still affordable, and there are now almost 70 of them.

Helen moved from New Orleans to LA in 2014 to get her MFA in screenwriting from USC. She then worked her way up from assistant to staffed writer, most recently working as a producer. In 2023 she was part of the writers guild strike. She saw firsthand how union solidarity was essential to our contract negotiation when the Teamsters refused to cross our picket line. Executives thought they could "bank" scripts (get writers to hand in scripts before the strike), and then they could just film things during the strike. But because the Teamsters wouldn't cross picket lines, production was shut down across the state and country. When unions band together in solidarity, they win.

In West Hollywood since 2016, Helen has steadily gotten more involved in the city's leadership, serving on the West Hollywood Transportation Commission and speaking out at City Council, Commissions, and Advisory Board Meetings. Here in WeHo Helen sees some of the same problems she saw in New Orleans in the aftermath of Katrina - a housing and affordability crisis that threatens the very culture of our city. But she's not afraid to roll up her sleeves and work with all our stakeholders to create more housing, to bring filming back to WeHo, to create safer, more connected streets, and to streamline permitting for all our businesses.
Helen believes that by all working together, we can write the next chapter of this incredible city.

text: West Hollywood has been one of the defining places of my life. For more than twenty years, I have experienced this community through seasons of challenge, growth, and opportunity. Today, I am running for City Council because I believe in giving back to the city that has given me so much.

My journey has not been ordinary. I have experienced homelessness, battled addiction, and rebuilt my life one day at a time. Today, after more than eleven years of sobriety, I know that lasting change is possible. I know the dignity that comes from being seen, supported, and given the opportunity to rebuild in a community that believes people are more than the hardest chapter of their lives. I also know the importance of taking responsibility for the life you build next. Those experiences continue to shape how I listen, how I lead, and how I approach public service.

Like many of my neighbors, I rent an apartment, work in our local small business community, and experience the everyday realities of life in West Hollywood. I have spent years listening to seniors, longtime residents, local business owners, and neighbors from every walk of life. Those conversations have taught me that the best government listens first, plans thoughtfully, and earns the public's trust.

I am a retail sales associate, award-winning author, and actor. I earned degrees from New York University, Harvard University, and the University of Cambridge, and I am currently completing my Master of Public Administration at the USC Sol Price School of Public Policy. My education taught me how government works. My life taught me who government should work for.

As your Councilmember, I will work to strengthen public safety, support housing that is affordable while planning responsibly for our future, help local businesses thrive, address homelessness with compassion, accountability, real solutions, and the perspective of lived experience, and ensure City Hall is transparent, fiscally responsible, and responsive to the people it serves.
I believe our city is strongest when every resident feels heard, every neighborhood has a voice, and every decision is guided by transparency, respect, and a commitment to working together.
Together, we can build a West Hollywood that honors its past, embraces its present, and prepares responsibly for its future. It would be the honor of my life to earn your trust and your vote.

text: When Jonathan Cottrell first visited West Hollywood at 24 years old, he knew he had found his home. Jonathan and his husband Erik own and operate a local sports bar and community gathering spot (GYM Bar Weho) and are raising their newborn son here in the city they love.

West Hollywood is at a real inflection point, with two longtime pioneers leaving the City Council. Jonathan is running to preserve what we love about West Hollywood; address and rethink solutions to the challenges we face; and work to position our city for the future.

Jonathan will work to tackle the affordability crisis affecting all of us: renters, homeowners, small businesses, and workers alike. He believes we grow economic opportunity by attracting high-quality jobs and welcoming creative and green small businesses.
As a business owner himself, Jonathan is both pro-worker and pro-small business, because it's good for our community when everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

Jonathan is pro-housing and will support more affordable homes/apartments that are concentrated on commercial corridors, and transit nodes where the infrastructure can support it. He'll also build on our legacy of strong tenant protections and stabilization policies.

Above all, Jonathan believes public office is a public trust. At a time when confidence in government is at an all-time low across the board, Jonathan believes West Hollywood should do what we always do - raise the bar. This includes: setting clear goals, tracking outcomes, and showing residents the results. Jonathan will advance accountability, starting with himself. He'll keep his own phone off the dais so residents always have his full attention during meetings, and he hopes his colleagues will join him in that commitment. He'll also look at strengthening financial disclosures for our public officials, because residents should never have to wonder or worry about whether out-of-state billionaires are influencing decisions here at home, and they have every right to know who is funding their local government.
Please consider voting for Jonathan Cottrell for one of the three seats on the City Council. To learn more, visit cottrell4weho.com.
Jonathan Cottrell

text: WeHo can't wait! We need bold leaders who will protect the welcoming and diverse community that so many of us are proud to call home.

I, Stephen Post, am a renter, nonprofit advocate, business improvement manager, and West Hollywood Public Safety Commissioner. Throughout my career, I've worked to advance criminal justice reform, strengthen local communities, and bring residents, businesses, and public officials together to solve difficult problems. I've organized community dialogues on topics such as drug reform, race relations, and community policing - training more than 50 moderators and engaging nearly 500 community members, students, local officials, and law enforcement officers. As a WeHo 2040 Strategic Plan team-member, I've gathered community input from our residents that will directly shape the next 15 years of our city.

ln my current full-time role as a Business Improvement District manager, I work directly with local LA neighborhoods to support over 300 small/local businesses, strengthen neighborhood infrastructure, and help make our streets cleaner and safer. I've also spent years advocating for criminal justice reform and fairer cannabis laws, and my career in advocacy has helped seal over 200,000 records in California.

As an Area Planning Commissioner, I've advanced different development projects by prioritizing community needs and input. While earning my Master's of Public Administration at The Ohio State University, I served as President representing over 13,000 graduate students; winning annual increases of worker wages, protecting immigrant families from being evicted during COVID-19, and ensuring adequate benefits for our most vulnerable.

I'll stand up for WeHo by increasing funding to homelessness prevention, implementing a rent reduction for stabilized units, expanding public affordable housing options, improving community safety, and making City Hall more transparent and accountable.

West Hollywood was founded by LGBTQ+ rights advocates and tenants rights advocates who refused to remain invisible. We can't be afraid to build on their progress by supporting our legacy businesses, investing in climate-resilient infrastructure, and giving residents a stronger voice in how their dollars are spent. This City has always shown what progressive leadership can accomplish. The future is up to us now. I hope to earn your vote and continue building the thriving city we are supposed to be.

text: I'm Kevin Ligon, a retired civil servant, and I'm asking for your vote for West Hollywood City Council.

As a Program Manager at the VA Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System, I helped more than 75,000 veterans access online services and trained over 10,000 healthcare employees. Earlier in my career, I worked in marketing and communications, helping startup companies launch new products and grow their businesses. These experiences taught me how to solve problems, build consensus, and develop practical, creative solutions. Before receiving my Masters in Communication, I was a Financial Planner helping individuals and small businesses invest, obtain loans, and create business plans to reach their goals. Throughout my career, I have helped technology companies, television networks - TBS, TNT, TNT Latin America and National Geographic - and the Department of Veterans Affairs communicate with the people they serve.

I was inspired to run for City Council by my neighbors and fellow Tenant Association members. For the past 15 years, I have lived in an apartment building with residents of many ages, backgrounds, and perspectives. I have seen firsthand the challenges that arise in tenant-landlord relationships and the emotional stress people experience when concerns about maintenance, safety, noise, or changes to their homes threaten their peace of mind. Everyone deserves to feel secure in the place they call home.

I also see too many empty storefronts where thriving local businesses once served our community. We must do more to help entrepreneurs and small businesses fill these spaces, strengthen our local economy, and preserve the vibrant character that makes West Hollywood unique.

As your Councilmember, I will listen carefully, lead with integrity, and make decisions based on transparency, fiscal responsibility, and collaboration. I will work to strengthen our neighborhoods, support local businesses, and ensure that West Hollywood remains a safe, welcoming, and vibrant city for residents of every generation.
I've spent my career in service to others. On Election Day, I'll be asking for the chance to serve you. Vote Kevin Ligon.
For more information: www.kevinligon.com

text: Being a resident of the proudest city in America, I'm excited to run for West Hollywood City Council and address the diverse wants and needs of our residents and local business owners.

As the son of Cuban refugees, I saw firsthand that hard work, dedication and persistence led my parents to achieve a better life for our family of 7. That same work ethic drove me to start my own small business right in the heart of West Hollywood, OPVS. A neighborhood gym that evolved into a safe space for the community to come together, get strong and feel seen.

I hold a B.S. in Political Science which I'll use to shape public policy that can better the daily lives of our residents and businesses. I also hold a B.A. in International Studies and find myself in a unique position to understand the multicultural diversity that makes up our great city.

Small businesses are fundamental to a thriving community. I will spearhead the creation of a Commercial Rent Stabilization Division to tackle the ever-increasing price of goods and services, driven by a largely speculative and greedy commercial market. Small business owners are being strong armed into leases that force their hand into increasing prices to our residents. I will take immediate action to stop this endless cycle.

Safety is paramount. Safety for our seniors, our marginalized communities, our Russian speaking residents, our businesses and our tourist economy. I will champion the creation of the West Hollywood Police Department. We have become too reliant on Los Angeles for our policing. Our city's needs are multifaceted, and our police force needs to reflect the complex relationship many in our community have already experienced.

I will pioneer the creation of the UPP (Universal Parking Pass) for city residents. We need a complete overhaul of our Residential Parking Division. Aggressive ticketing practices create an unaffordable burden on our community. Our streets have become a complex web of signs that all too often act as a punishment and not a privilege to our residents.

To know me is to understand that my deep sense of personal responsibility and work ethic is rooted in my love for my partner, my children, my friends, and this beautiful city I call home. I hope to be lucky enough to garner your support and your vote in this upcoming election. Please visit www.joel4weho.com or email: vote@joel4weho.com

text: My name is Tom DeMille, a 35-year resident of West Hollywood running to give our city back to its residents. For too long, the people of our community have been ignored. As a result, residents no longer attend city meetings or help guide council members on critical decisions. When I first moved here, West Hollywood thrived on active democracy. We had passionate debates with hundreds of residents on opposing sides speaking out, compromising, and ultimately reaching a consensus where everyone felt heard. Today, that collaborative spirit is entirely absent.

Beyond governance, public safety in our city is in shambles. I firmly believe that every resident and guest has the fundamental right to sleep peacefully at night without fear of break-ins, and to feel completely safe strolling down our boulevards at any hour of the day or night.

My commitment to this city is proven by my actions when no one was looking. Following the tragedy of September 11th, West Hollywood lacked even a single flagpole. After organizing a candlelight vigil attended by 4,000 residents the next day, I spent 33 days waving the American flag on the site where the Veterans Memorial now stands (this year will be the 25th anniversary of 9/11) to offer comfort and security to our community. That effort ultimately led to the installation of roughly 100 flagpoles across our city, including the one proudly standing in front of the Sheriffs' station.

With your support, I will transform our city into a lasting legacy by creating three distinct Walk of Fame tributes: the Gay Icon Walk of Fame, the Sunset Music Icon Walk of Fame, and a memorial East of Fairfax honoring the Russian war heroes who helped defeat Nazi Germany. This will make our city vibrant for the next 100 years, ensuring we can pass down our local businesses to our children. This initiative requires minimal funding, as it can be integrated directly into necessary sidewalk repairs. Additionally, we will widen the sidewalks throughout the Rainbow District to create vibrant gathering spaces for our community rather than forcing people onto the roadside. After 35 years of marching, our residents deserve dedicated spaces to assemble.
In closing, when elected, I will defend every resident and guest who comes into our city with my life, so help me God. I ask for your vote.

Thank you,
The Legacy Candidate

text: West Hollywood has been my home for 36 years. I built my civil rights law practice here. It was an honor to serve on your Council from 2000-2020. Today, I'm running because the city needs experienced independent leadership focused on residents – not political ambitions.

In recent years, the new council has drifted from critical priorities. Political ideology, special interests and higher office ambition have trumped protecting our neighborhoods, supporting public safety and improving residents' quality of life.
I'm running to restore common sense and accountable leadership. With longtime Councilmembers John Heilman and Lauren Meister termed out, both encouraged me
to return and provide the experienced steady hand our city needs.

WeHo deserves thoughtful growth – not overdevelopment. Affordable housing includes protecting our rent-controlled apartments, preserving historic neighborhoods and keeping WeHo unique. I oppose eliminating traffic lanes on Fountain Avenue. Bike lanes belong down on Willoughby where they can better serve cyclists without reducing parking, interfering with first responders and jamming all our traffic arteries.

Public safety remains my top priority and I historically earned the endorsement of our sheriff deputies union. West Hollywood has many vulnerable communities that require protection from hatred. Reducing law enforcement funding has weakened public safety. I will work to restore the full funding of our sheriffs and fire departments.

We must rebuild the torn relationship between our city and chamber of commerce. Our restaurants, hotels, nightclubs and entertainment venues are essential to our economy and identity. This symbiotic relationship must be renewed to reduce storefront vacancies and strengthen our neighborhoods.

Finally, we must confront homelessness with both compassion and a firm hand. We should continue to help those who want services. But we must also remove those individuals with severe mental health episodes who bring criminality onto our city streets and threaten residents and businesses alike.

During my 20 years of council service, I created the West Hollywood Recovery Center site and protection for the Log Cabin 12 step meeting facility. I created the free nighttime shuttle, rainbow crosswalks, neighborhood dog parks, AIDS monument and new design for West Hollywood Park, pool and library. I tripled the budget for our fine arts programming and required adequate parking for all proposed new developments. I have a record of tenant protections under our ordinance and building long term prudent reserves for the city.
I respectfully ask for your vote to bring pragmatic common sense back to City Hall.

text: West Hollywood has shown what local leadership can accomplish by putting people first. From renter protections to civil rights to social services, our city has set an example for others to follow. As an LGBTQ+ resident, that legacy is personal. Protecting it also requires us to demand change when local government stops listening.

Today, too many residents feel decisions are made for them, not with them. They see their legitimate concerns dismissed, public meetings held after outcomes are already decided, and political theater replacing pragmatic solutions and compromise. We need a City Council that listens, not lectures, and that gives residents a meaningful voice in shaping outcomes.

That is why I am running: not to build a political career, but to bring fact-based, community-focused leadership back to West Hollywood. My career in finance has taught me to make disciplined budget decisions, weigh competing priorities, ask difficult questions, and measure results. I will bring that same discipline to each City Council decision. Every taxpayer dollar should have a purpose, every city program should have clear goals and transparent reporting, and the public should be heard before major decisions are made, not after.

Good leadership rejects the false choices that too often dominate local politics. We can address crime while protecting civil rights and privacy. We can support fair labor practices while helping local businesses open, fill empty storefronts, and succeed.

That approach already guides my advocacy on behalf of our residents before City Council. I have called for a local development plan that welcomes new housing without displacing renters, eliminating rent-stabilized homes, or ignoring neighborhood character and infrastructure. I opposed the Fountain Avenue redesign as proposed and advocated for less disruptive alternatives that improve safety and protect all road users without worsening congestion or removing needed residential parking.

Across city issues, my approach will remain consistent: listen before deciding, ground decisions in evidence and real-world impacts, measure results, and change course when a policy is not serving our community. West Hollywood's strongest leadership has combined bold values with officials that are responsive to public input. I am running to restore that balance, make City Council work with the community, and hold it accountable for results.

I respectfully ask for your vote to so we can put residents at the center of City Council decisions and deliver pragmatic, considerate, and accountable leadership for everyone who calls West Hollywood home.

text: I'm Councilmember Chelsea Byers, and in 2022, I ran on the belief that a transformative agenda could deliver a more livable, caring, and connected community. Over my four years as Councilmember and Mayor, I have worked with our community to get real wins on affordability, sustainability, and safety while building a city that's diverse and inclusive for generations to come.

During my first term, I've built relationships with decision-makers across Los Angeles County to tackle the urgent issues facing our residents. These regional connections have delivered funding, partnerships, and new opportunities back to West Hollywood while ensuring our city has a voice in the decisions that affect us. I'm proud of the track record I have as a result:
Led the effort to strengthen our rent stabilization ordinance and accelerated the creation of new affordable housing.
Helped launch the financial mechanism that will generate $2.2 billion for the creation of Metro's K Line Northern Extension, bringing three Metro stations to West Hollywood
Championed the expansion of West Hollywood's child care initiatives and increased social services funding by $1 million.
Co-authored a motion establishing ICE-free zones on city-owned property.
Enhanced streetscape projects by adding protected bike lanes and expanding mobility options to improve safety for pedestrians and cyclists.
Launched the "WeHo Loves Locals Gift Card" program, increasing investment in West Hollywood's business community.

With state funding cuts, families feeling the strain of the affordability crisis, and a Trump administration threatening our rights and freedoms, we can't afford business as usual. As a young, queer renter and transit user, I know we need leaders who will take on tough fights: to lower housing costs, strengthen social services, modernize our aging infrastructure, make our streets safer and easier to navigate, and tackle the climate crisis with the urgency it demands.
We must protect what we have built, fix what is broken, and create new opportunities for all those who call West Hollywood home. I would be honored to earn your vote once more.

I am proud to be supported by a broad coalition of individuals and organizations including Los Angeles County Supervisor Lindsey Horvath, Congressmember Laura Friedman, Los Angeles County Assessor Jeff Prang, Los Angeles/Orange Counties Building & Construction Trades Council, the California Working Families Party, and Stonewall Democratic Club among others. Learn more at chelsea4weho.com

text: West Hollywood thrives on bold vision, authentic expression, and collaborative leadership. As an international fashion designer and creative director, I have spent my career turning ambitious ideas into reality by balancing artistic execution with rigorous operational strategy. My journey began with years of intensive art and design study at London's Central Saint Martins, followed by serving as Director of Operations for Thom Browne as well a Liaison to NASA's next generation space suit study.

When I launched my eponymous brand, MARLON GOBEL, it demanded absolute strategic precision along with skills that translated into immediate global partnerships with historic institutions like Bergdorf Goodman, Swarovski, and the Fashion Institute of Technology. Over a twenty-year career, my work has been recognized by The New York Times and trusted by legendary creative icons, because I deliver on bold ideas, resilience, and unique innovation.

I am running for City Council because West Hollywood deserves leadership that understands how to manage complex operations while preserving our distinct, rebellious, and authentic spirit. I will bring fiscal discipline, project management expertise, and an unwavering dedication to making our community a vibrant, sustainable, and forward-thinking destination for residents and creators alike. I would be honored to earn your vote. Let's build the future of WeHo together.

text: I'm seeking to be elected to the City Council of the City of West Hollywood. I'm a proud West Hollywood resident for 22 years. It's been an honor to serve my community as a nonprofit leader, as a technology leader, as an activist and volunteer. I bring decades of experience in strategic thinking, creating change and listening with compassion. In the corporate world, I've created project plans and led teams of various sizes. In the nonprofit word, I've helped launch new programs and increased membership, while navigating economic instability to create protections for the future. In both fields, I've helped create growth, stability and a culture of belonging.

I couldn't have done any of this without my West Hollywood community. Countless coffee runs with friends, marches, community gatherings, and walks around our neighborhood to clear my head. We have created something truly special in West Hollywood – a community that needs to be valued and preserved.

In order to do so, we must listen to residents. Listening does not end after Election Day. It is my job and a great privilege to listen to the residents of West Hollywood, to build consensus around goals, to find common ground when there are disagreements and to be transparent when a goal can't be achieved.

We've witnessed many changes over the years, and more changes are coming. It is critical that we prepare for growth, while preserving the core community values that have made West Hollywood a beacon of hope.
Lastly: my name is Nigerian and is pronounced CHEE-ed-oo ee-BOO-nee-way.
Don't ever be afraid to ask me how to say it. I won't be offended.

text: West Hollywood deserves a City Hall that puts residents first. Common sense should never be political. As a nonprofit executive, I have dedicated myself to serving others, solving problems, and bringing people together. My commitment to community began when I founded my high school's first Gay-Straight Alliance, and it continues today through public service.

I am running because local government should answer to the people of West Hollywood before Sacramento. Development must be done with a progressive mindset while respecting the current residents and their way of life. In doing so, we need to invest in bringing back our vibrant business community by cutting the red tape, and incentivizing growth and investment in our town. Public safety must be our highest priority. Every resident deserves clean streets, safe neighborhoods, thriving parks, and a city where businesses can succeed. We must support law enforcement, address homelessness with compassion and accountability, and reduce unnecessary barriers that make it harder for local businesses to grow.
I will listen, lead with integrity, and always put residents first. Together, we can build a safer, stronger, and more prosperous West Hollywood that works for everyone.
I respectfully ask for your vote.
